metadata.note: Caltrain, from the Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board's takeover on July 1 1992 to the 2026 GTFS pull. The Southern Pacific ran the same trains (subsidised by Caltrans from 1980, branded CalTrain from 1985) until June 30 1992; that era is in sf_san_jose_railroad.geojson. Contract operators: Amtrak 1992-2012, TransitAmerica Services from May 26 2012. The colour follows the agency, not the contractor. Weekday train counts per era are from Caltrain's milestones and Wikipedia; headway_min is 1440 / weekday trains (both directions), the same convention as the GTFS-derived 2026 figure.
metadata.caltrain_audit_2026_10_14: Rebuilt. The four 2026-only service-pattern features (Local Weekday, Local Weekend, Limited, Express), drawn as straight lines between stations with up to 10 mi chords and no geometry note, and with a placeholder 1440-minute weekend headway, were collapsed into one OSM-traced San Francisco - San Jose feature whose 2026 segment carries the GTFS pattern counts. Service now runs from July 1 1992 instead of 2026 only, filling the 1986-2025 gap (SP's era now runs to June 30 1992). The Gilroy feature was retraced; its geometry_repairs record listed one repair twice and its note double-counted the mileage.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

properties.speed_source: computed from 150 scheduled Local trips, GTFS stop_times (2026); earlier eras assume the same
properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap 2026-10-14 along ways named 'Caltrain Peninsula Subdivision' (Dijkstra over railway=rail, mainline-preferred, no bridged gaps). 46.8 mi from 4th and King to San Jose Diridon, against 46.7 mi by Caltrain's mileposts (MP 0.2 - 46.9).

segments.note: The Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board took over on July 1 1992, with Amtrak as contract operator, and raised weekday service from 54 to 60 trains. Caltrain's milestones record further increases in the later 1990s (not re-checked here); headway_min uses the July 1992 count.
sources: Segment-level: July 1 1992 takeover and 60 weekday trains checked against Caltrain's 1990s milestones page.

segments.note: Weekday service cut from 80 to 76 trains in August 2002; weekend service suspended July 2002 to June 2004 for the CTX track works.
sources: Segment-level: checked against Caltrain's 2000s milestones page.

segments.note: Baby Bullet express service began in June 2004. The 86-train count is from Caltrain's milestones as reported to this project and was not re-checked.
sources: NOT SOURCED AT SEGMENT LEVEL: the 2004 count was not re-checked against the page below.

segments.note: From August 2005 the schedule had 22 Baby Bullets and 96 weekday trains.
sources: Segment-level: checked against Caltrain's 2000s milestones page.

segments.note: Wikipedia gives a cut from 90 to 86 weekday trains on January 1 2011 and 92 before the COVID-19 pandemic; headway_min uses 90. TransitAmerica Services replaced Amtrak as contract operator on May 26 2012.

segments.note: COVID-19 cuts: 42 weekday trains from March 30 2020, 70 from June 15 and 68 from December 14; headway_min uses 68.

segments.note: 70 weekday trains until August 30 2021, then 104 with the Baby Bullets restored.

segments.note: Electric service: the first EMUs carried passengers in August 2024 and diesel trains were retired September 21 2024. 104 weekday trains (52 each way); weekends doubled to 66 trains, locals every 30 minutes.
sources: Segment-level: checked against Wikipedia's Caltrain article.

segments.note: GTFS pulled 2026-08-17, representative Wednesday: 75 Local, 15 Limited and 14 Express trips (both directions), San Francisco - San Jose Diridon. Weekends 66 Local trips, extended to Tamien. avg_speed_kmh is the Local's (54.2); the Limited averages 64.2 and the Express 74.8.
sources: Segment-level: trip counts and speeds computed from the agency GTFS feed.
